root_cause.text: The allocation for `scontrol->ipc_control_data` used the topology-provided `max_size` (which only accounts for `sof_abi_hdr` + payload) but omitted the size of the kernel-only `struct sof_ipc4_control_data`, causing an undersized buffer and out-of-bounds write when the full control data is stored.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `kzalloc(scontrol->max_size, GFP_KERNEL)` to `kzalloc(sizeof(*control_data) + scontrol->max_size, GFP_KERNEL)`, explicitly adding the missing struct size. The commit message states: "With the change we will allocate [1] amount more memory to be able to hold the full size of data." The validation checks are also corrected to no longer subtract `sizeof(*control_data)` from `max_size`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix incorrect size checks and buffer allocation in sof_ipc4_control_load_bytes by properly accounting for the control_data header being separate from the max payload size.
intent_record.what: Modified the validation conditions: removed sizeof(*control_data) from the first and second checks, added a new check that priv_size must be at least sizeof(struct sof_abi_hdr), updated the size assignment to use sizeof(*control_data) (equivalent), and changed the allocation from kzalloc(scontrol->max_size, GFP_KERNEL) to kzalloc(sizeof(*control_data) + scontrol->max_size, GFP_KERNEL). Also added explanatory comments.
intent_record.how: The minimum required max_size is reduced because it no longer needs to accommodate the control_data header. The allowed initial data size (priv_size) can now be up to max_size (previously limited to max_size - sizeof(control_data)). A lower bound for priv_size is enforced. The allocation now correctly includes space for the control_data structure plus the max payload, fixing a potential buffer overflow. The actual size field remains unchanged.

relevance_review.reason: The group's core intent directly addresses the vulnerability root cause by fixing the buffer allocation to properly include the size of the control_data header, which was previously omitted, leading to an undersized buffer.
